explanations: terra: The humble are characterized by conviction that they will meet their Lord and return to Him, giving the faceward movement both an encounter and a return.

luna: The source section says face can stand for the whole person; «أسلم وجهه لله وهو محسن» combines surrender of self with good action and promises its reward, making the image practical. | terra: مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُۥ لِلَّهِ uses the face for the surrendered self and promises security from fear and grief, illustrating the section's “face as person” sense.

luna: The source section treats وجه as both the front toward which one turns and God's own self; «فأينما تولوا فثم وجه الله» makes turning and God's face meet in a concise formulation. | terra: فَأَيْنَمَا تُوَلُّوا۟ فَثَمَّ وَجْهُ ٱللَّهِ makes every act of turning a possible orientation toward God's face, precisely joining the two key word-images.

terra: Other communities will not be pleased until the Prophet follows their way, while the ayah identifies God's guidance as the true guidance; the object whose pleasure is sought can redirect the follower.

luna: The source section distinguishes turning toward from turning away; this qibla passage asks «ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم» and says God guides whom He wills to a straight path, introducing the direction change expanded in 2:143-144. | terra: The qiblah passage opens with the question مَا وَلَّىٰهُمْ عَن قِبْلَتِهِمُ: what turned them away from their former direction, preparing the commanded turn of 2:144.

luna: The source section reads turning as bodily direction and response to a command; the qibla is made a test of who follows the Messenger, and 2:144 completes the scene with the Prophet's face and the new direction. | terra: The qiblah is made a test distinguishing one who follows the Messenger from one who يَنقَلِبُ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ, turning back on his heels rather than accepting the new direction.

luna: The source section says the Qur'an gathers turning, face, and pleasure here: Allah sees the Prophet's face turn heavenward, grants a qibla he is pleased with, and commands him to turn his face toward the Sacred Mosque. | terra: The ayah gathers all three movements developed in the section: the Prophet's face turns repeatedly toward heaven, God turns him to a qiblah he will be pleased with, and commands فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ toward it.

luna: The source section makes face-direction an act of allegiance; this neighbor says the scriptural communities will not follow the Prophet's qibla and warns against following their desires, adding the boundary around 2:144's command. | terra: The People of the Book will not follow the Prophet's qiblah, nor he theirs, setting faithful face-direction against competing orientations and desire-led following.

luna: The source section cites turning toward as one sense of و ل ي; «ولكل وجهة هو موليها» uses that direction sense and immediately commands racing toward good deeds, linking orientation to action. | terra: وَلِكُلٍّ وِجْهَةٌ هُوَ مُوَلِّيهَا gives each community a direction toward which it turns and immediately commands a race in good deeds, joining orientation with energetic pursuit.

luna: The source section uses the Prophet's face turning toward the qibla as an example of positive tawallī; this ayah repeats the command for wherever he sets out and says it leaves no argument, extending 2:144's direction. | terra: The repeated command فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ makes the bodily face carry an obedient direction beyond the first command in 2:144.

luna: The source section develops turning the face toward a chosen direction; this ayah universalizes the qibla command to wherever believers are, completing the scene begun in 2:144 and reiterated in 2:149. | terra: The qiblah command is extended to the Prophet and community wherever they are, so many faces share the same deliberate direction.
terra: Disbelievers are likened to animals hearing only a caller's cry and sound, a herd scene that makes failure to listen and understand perceptible.

luna: The source section develops turning the face as orientation toward God; this ayah marks a boundary: turning faces east or west by itself is not righteousness, which instead includes faith, giving, prayer, and keeping commitments. | terra: Righteousness is not merely أَن تُوَلُّوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمْ east or west; faith and generous action give bodily direction its moral content, a precise boundary on the section's face imagery.

luna: The source section's root ب غ ي/B001 means seeking, and its «وجه ربه» is God Himself; this person gives himself up «ابتغاء مرضات الله», a close parallel in which the sought divine approval governs the whole self. | terra: A person sells his very self ٱبْتِغَآءَ مَرْضَاتِ ٱللَّهِ, so the search for divine pleasure takes the whole person rather than only the face as a bodily part.

luna: The source section says the giver expects no human recompense; this verse describes spending without following it with reminders or injury, protecting the recipient from being made indebted to the giver.

luna: The source section rejects seeking repayment or gratitude from recipients; this verse says kind speech and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury, sharpening the ethical form of giving.

luna: The source section's giver seeks Allah's face alone; this verse warns that charity done to be seen by people and followed by reminders can be nullified, a specific reversal of that intention. | terra: Charity spoiled by reminders, injury, and being seen by people reverses the unrecompensed, face-seeking gift: the outward act remains while its gaze is fixed on a human audience.

luna: The source section names ب غ ي/B001 as seeking and ر ض و/B001 as approval; this verse directly joins spending wealth with seeking Allah's pleasure and pictures that intention as a garden on high ground, adding a cultivated image to the section's giving. | terra: Those who spend their wealth ٱبْتِغَآءَ مَرْضَاتِ ٱللَّهِ unite strenuous seeking, giving, and God's pleasure, the same sequence that runs from 92:18 through 92:21.

luna: The source section's phrase ابتغاء وجه ربه names seeking God's face; here Allah joins the Prophet's limited responsibility for guidance to believers' spending only to seek His face, making intention and guidance meet in one instruction. | terra: The ayah joins guidance, spending, and the exact motive إِلَّا ٱبْتِغَآءَ وَجْهِ ٱللَّهِ, closely reproducing the section's movement from God's guidance to giving solely in search of His face.
terra: Those who spend their wealth by night and day, secretly and openly, bring together the two pairs that the section explicitly connects: night/day and hidden/open giving.

luna: The source section names ب غ ي/B001 as seeking with effort toward God; here the same source-section root appears in seeking discord and an interpretation, a specific contrary aim that shows the sought object matters.

luna: The source section's idea of turning toward God appears as «أسلمت وجهي لله»; the speaker's submission makes the face a declaration of allegiance, not merely a direction of sight. | terra: “I have surrendered my face to God” is followed in the same ayah by فَإِن تَوَلَّوْا۟: submission turns the whole self toward God, while refusal turns away from the message.

luna: The source section makes the Lord the object of seeking; this ayah warns against seeking another religion, «يبتغ غير الإسلام دينا», and gives that rival orientation no acceptance. | terra: Whoever يَبْتَغِ a religion other than submission will not have it accepted; effortful seeking does not save a search aimed away from the accepted direction.
terra: The question whether believers would turn back on their heels if Muhammad died makes bodily reversal the image of abandoning a commitment after its guide is lost.

luna: The source section contrasts the face that seeks with the one turned away; «يردوكم على أعقابكم» warns that others can turn believers back on their heels and make them retreat from their chosen direction.

luna: The source section sets two orientations against one another; this battle ayah says some wanted the world and some the Hereafter after disobeying, while 3:153 depicts the fleeing that turns from the caller.

luna: The source section's root و ل ي/B007 includes turning away physically and ceasing to heed; here people flee uphill «ولا تلون على أحد» while the Messenger calls behind them, a sharp scene of not turning back to the caller. | terra: The believers climb away without turning toward anyone while the Messenger calls them from behind, combining bodily retreat, a voice left at their backs, and failure to respond.

luna: The source section defines ر ض و/B001 as the opposite of anger; this ayah explicitly contrasts following God's approval with incurring His wrath, clarifying the stakes of the final يرضى. | terra: The ayah explicitly opposes following رِضْوَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ to returning with God's سَخَط, exactly enacting the dictionary statement that رضى is the contrary of anger.

luna: The source section's root ر ض و/B001 describes contentment and approval; after danger, these people follow Allah's pleasure and return with grace and no harm, showing approval as an orienting aim under pressure. | terra: The believers return with grace and no harm after وَٱتَّبَعُوا۟ رِضْوَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ; divine pleasure is something followed through fearful circumstances.
terra: Obeying the Messenger is obedience to God, while مَن تَوَلَّىٰ marks rejection of that obedience; the Messenger is not appointed as their keeper.
luna: The source section's search is for the Lord rather than a return; this ayah warns fighters against «تبتغون عرض الحياة الدنيا», exposing worldly gain as a competing object of pursuit.
terra: Secret counsel becomes good when it orders charity, recognized good, or reconciliation and is done ٱبْتِغَآءَ مَرْضَاتِ ٱللَّهِ, showing concrete deeds directed solely at divine approval.

terra: After guidance has become clear, one who opposes the Messenger and follows another path is left to what he has turned toward; guidance, chosen route, and the two-directional root meet in one warning.

luna: The source section says وجه may stand for the person himself; the good-doer who «أسلم وجهه لله» offers the whole self to God, directly clarifying the phrase's force beyond bodily orientation. | terra: The best religion is attributed to one who أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُۥ لِلَّهِ while doing good, again making face both the self and its Godward orientation.

luna: The source section names ب غ ي/B001 as seeking and ر ض و/B001 as contentment; this ayah describes pilgrims «يبتغون ... رضوانا», bringing effortful seeking and divine approval into one scene. | terra: Travelers heading for the Sacred House are described as يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَرِضْوَٰنًا, so physical destination and the search for divine pleasure coincide.

luna: The source section joins seeking God's face to guidance; here Allah guides those who seek His approval «سبل السلام», taking them from darkness to light and to a straight path. | terra: God guides those who follow His pleasure into paths of peace and out of darkness into light, turning رضوان into a followed direction rather than a static feeling.
terra: Moses commands his people to enter the holy land and not turn back on their heels lest they return as losers, opposing forward obedience to ruinous reversal.
terra: وَٱبْتَغُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِ ٱلْوَسِيلَةَ is paired with striving in God's path, making seeking toward Him an active, effortful orientation.
terra: Obedience to God and the Messenger is commanded, and فَإِن تَوَلَّيْتُمْ leaves the Messenger responsible only for clear delivery, again defining the turn as refused command.

luna: The source section's root ر ض و/B001 marks contentment; this ayah says Allah is pleased with the truthful and they are pleased with Him, in the judgment scene that closes the preceding account. | terra: On the Day truthfulness benefits the truthful, رَّضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا۟ عَنْهُ makes satisfaction reciprocal between Lord and servants.
terra: Whenever a sign from their Lord comes, the people turn away from it; the next ayah identifies this repeated aversion as denial of the truth.
terra: The people deny the truth when it reaches them, completing the turn-away scene of 6:4 and promising that news of what they mocked will reach them in return.

luna: The source section says the sought «وجه» is God Himself; this ayah describes people who call on their Lord morning and evening «يريدون وجهه», making that orientation a settled practice. | terra: Those who call on their Lord morning and evening يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ keep their attention fixed on the sought face across the day's recurring turns.

luna: The source section's search keeps its gaze fixed on the sought one; Abraham rejects the setting star with «لا أحب الآفلين», and the next ayat carry his inquiry through moon and sun before he turns to their Creator.
luna: The source section connects seeking God's face with guidance; Abraham says he would be among the lost without his Lord's guidance, while 6:79 states the face he finally turns toward.
luna: The source section's image is a face directed to God rather than elsewhere; after the sun sets Abraham disavows association, and 6:79 names his turn toward the Creator.

luna: The source section describes وجه as direction and as God's own self; after rejecting the star, moon, and sun in 6:76-78, Abraham says «وجهت وجهي» toward the Creator, naming his chosen direction. | terra: Abraham declares إِنِّى وَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِىَ toward the Creator of the heavens and earth, an exact Quranic enactment of the section's idiom “I turned my face to God.”
terra: The ayah describes the worst wrong as denying God's signs and turning aside from them, explicitly coupling takdhīb with a refusal to face the guidance and mercy that have arrived.
luna: The source section says وجه can stand for the person himself; here the speaker says his prayer, worship, life, and death belong to Allah, making whole-person dedication explicit.

luna: The source section explains وجه as a direction and as the self; «أقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد» joins bodily orientation at worship to sincerity of religion, making the two senses work together. | terra: The command أَقِيمُوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمْ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ and sincere invocation turns the face bodily and the religion inwardly toward the same addressee.
luna: The source section's face image gives a direction toward God; this verse depicts people blocking paths and seeking to make God's way crooked, a specific reversal of the straight orientation.
terra: The man given God's signs slips out of them and is pursued by Satan; this withdrawal prepares the dog image and denial named in 7:176.

terra: The one who clings to earth and follows desire is likened to a panting dog, and the ayah identifies this as the likeness of those who كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا; denial is again made perceptible as animal behavior.
terra: People with ears that do not hear and eyes that do not see are likened to livestock and called heedless, expanding the section's turn-by-nonlistening into an animal analogy.

luna: The source section treats turning as a bodily act; the command «فلا تولوهم الأدبار» forbids turning one's back in battle, and 8:16 names the exception and the consequence of retreat. | terra: Believers meeting an advancing force are forbidden to تُوَلُّوهُمُ ٱلْأَدْبَارَ, a literal bodily turning of backs with moral consequence.

luna: The source section names و ل ي/B007 as turning away with the body or by abandoning obedience; this ayah calls bodily retreat «يوليهم يومئذ دبره» and says it incurs God's wrath, the inverse of seeking His approval. | terra: The ayah defines the narrow tactical exceptions to turning one's back in battle and otherwise ties that bodily turn to divine anger.

luna: The source section's و ل ي/B007 includes leaving listening and compliance; this command says not to turn away from Allah and His Messenger «وأنتم تسمعون», explicitly joining the bodily verb to hearing and obedience. | terra: Believers are commanded to obey God and His messenger and not تَوَلَّوْا۟ عَنْهُ while they hear, directly defining turning away as failure to heed rather than merely bodily motion.

luna: The source section's root و ل ي/B007 includes turning away by ceasing to heed; this ayah distinguishes people who merely say they hear from those who actually hear, following the command not to turn away while listening in 8:20. | terra: The warning not to resemble people who say “we hear” while they do not hear spells out the refused listening implicit in the turning of 8:20.
terra: Even if God made the unresponsive hear, لَتَوَلَّوا۟ وَّهُم مُّعْرِضُونَ; hearing followed by deliberate aversion exactly illustrates the section's nonbodily sense of tawallī.

luna: The source section describes turning away as failure to heed and comply; after 8:20-21 warns against that refusal, this ayah commands believers to respond when Allah and the Messenger call them to what gives life.
terra: At Hunayn the believers' numbers do not avail them and they وَلَّيْتُم مُّدْبِرِينَ, a concrete collective scene of bodies turning back under pressure.
terra: أَرَضِيتُم بِٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا مِنَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ rebukes people who cling heavily to the earth instead of moving out, a wrong satisfaction that halts the required journey.
terra: People swear to please the believers, but God and His messenger have the stronger claim to be pleased, distinguishing human approval from the proper object of the search.

luna: The source section ends with يرضى, contentment; here Allah's «رضوان» is declared greater than the gardens and dwellings, showing divine approval as the highest reward. | terra: After promised gardens and dwellings, وَرِضْوَٰنٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ makes God's approval the greater destination beyond the visible rewards.
terra: Some covenant that if God gives from His bounty they will surely give charity and become righteous; 9:76 exposes their later stinginess and turn as a reversal of this promised direction.
terra: When God grants them bounty, they become stingy with it and turn away in aversion, joining the miser's refusal to give with the bodily and inward turn found in surah 92.
terra: The broken promise and repeated lying of 9:75-76 leave hypocrisy in their hearts until the day they meet God, carrying the failed giving-and-turning scene to an inverted encounter.
terra: Even if believers are pleased with the excuse-makers, God is not pleased with the defiantly disobedient, sharply separating human satisfaction from divine approval.

luna: The source section's root ر ض و/B001 names approval; this verse gives the early emigrants, helpers, and their faithful followers the reciprocal reward of Allah's pleasure and their pleasure in Him. | terra: The first emigrants, helpers, and faithful followers reach the reciprocal end رَّضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا۟ عَنْهُ after a life of committed following.

terra: A building founded on reverence and God's pleasure is set against one founded on a collapsing bank that falls into Hell, giving sought approval a stable direction and its opposite a literal fall.

terra: Those who do not hope for meeting God are رَضُوا۟ بِٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا and remain heedless, contrasting satisfaction that settles into the near life with satisfaction reached by seeking the Lord.
terra: Those who do good receive ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ and more, while gloom and humiliation do not cover their faces; the ayah brings the “best” denied in 92:9 into relation with the face sought in 92:20.

luna: The source section develops the face as a direction and an act of turning; the command «أقم وجهك للدين حنيفا» gives that orientation a religious object and excludes divided worship. | terra: The imperative أَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا commands a settled face-direction, the positive end of the section's two-sided turning.

luna: The source section sets the sought Lord against turning away; this verse describes people who hinder from God's path, seek to make it crooked, and disbelieve in the Hereafter, joining crooked direction to denial.
terra: Noah asks his people for no wealth, says his reward is only with God, and refuses to drive away those who will meet their Lord, combining no human payment with the awaited encounter.
terra: Lot's household is told to travel by night and let no one look back; the forbidden backward gaze gives a concrete boundary to the section's animal that stops and looks behind.

terra: The brothers expect يَخْلُ لَكُمْ وَجْهُ أَبِيكُمْ after removing Joseph; if “your father's face” denotes his undivided regard, it is a human and morally distorted analogue to seeking a face as the person’s attention.
terra: Jacob orders his sons to go and search carefully for Joseph and his brother and not despair, a sustained search for lost loved ones whose hope keeps it moving.
terra: The brothers' recognition “Are you indeed Joseph?” and Joseph's answer bring the search ordered in 12:87 to a face-to-face discovery.

luna: The source section's phrase ابتغاء وجه ربه is repeated in «ابتغاء وجه ربهم»; this ayah binds that aim to patience and spending in secret and openly, extending the image from direction to sustained conduct. | terra: Those who persevere ٱبْتِغَآءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِمْ and spend secretly and openly enact the section's effortful face-seeking through sustained action and giving.

luna: The source section quotes those who patiently seek their Lord's face in 13:22; this next ayah names the Gardens of Eden they enter with their righteous kin, continuing that seekers' promised outcome.
luna: The source section links patience with seeking the Lord's face in 13:22; here the angels greet the entrants with peace because of their patience, completing the neighboring account's reward.
terra: God guides إِلَيْهِ مَنْ أَنَابَ, so turning back to Him becomes the motion by which guidance acquires a direction.
luna: The source section turns toward the Lord; these people prefer the present life, hinder others from God's path, and seek to make it crooked, a specific reversal of the straight direction.
terra: The repeated command that Lot's family depart at night and not let anyone look back keeps rescue dependent on an undivided forward direction.
terra: A powerless dependent brings no good wherever his master directs him and is contrasted with one commanding justice on a straight path; directed movement is measured by the good it produces.

luna: The source section joins the Prophet's limited responsibility for guidance to people who turn away; this ayah says if they turn away, his duty is only clear delivery, repeating that limit in the context of refusal.
terra: Whoever desires only the immediate world receives a measured portion and ends in Hell; beside 17:19 it shows how the sought object determines the direction and end of striving.

luna: The source section describes seeking as effortful and ends with the seeker content; this verse speaks of one who desires the Hereafter and strives for it as a believer, whose effort is appreciated. | terra: Whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the striving due to it gives a direct nonlexical definition of the section's اِبْتِغَاء as desire joined to exertion.

luna: The source section presents the Lord as the sole object of seeking; the counterfactual «لابتغوا إلى ذي العرش سبيلا» says that even alleged rival gods would have to seek a way to the Throne's Lord.

luna: The source section says turning away can mean leaving attention; when remembrance of the Merciful is made alone, they «ولوا على أدبارهم نفورا», a bodily withdrawal joined to aversion from hearing. | terra: When the one Lord is mentioned in the Quran, the hearers turn their backs and flee in aversion; coverings on hearts and heaviness in ears make the bodily retreat also a refusal to listen.

luna: The source section's root ب غ ي/B001 describes seeking toward God; even those invoked besides Him «يبتغون إلى ربهم الوسيلة» and hope for mercy while fearing punishment, locating the true direction above every intermediary. | terra: The very beings invoked by others themselves يَبْتَغُونَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمُ ٱلْوَسِيلَةَ and compete in nearness, fixing both the sought direction and the exertion of approach.
terra: When favored, the human being turns away and distances himself by his side; bodily posture expresses inward refusal, while distress reverses his mood into despair.

luna: The source section's phrase seeking the Lord's face is repeated in «يريدون وجهه»; the command to stay with these worshippers and not let one's eyes pass beyond them for worldly adornment makes the competing direction explicit. | terra: The Prophet is told to keep with those who call on their Lord morning and evening يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ and not let his eyes pass beyond them, explicitly combining face-seeking with disciplined gaze.

luna: The source section's account of turning away includes refusing to attend to a command; this ayah describes someone reminded by the Lord's signs who «فأعرض عنها», making the object of that refusal explicit. | terra: The person reminded of God's signs then turns away and forgets what his hands sent ahead; coverings over hearts and heaviness in ears spell out the refusal to hear within that turn.

luna: The source section says seeking by ابتغاء requires effort; Moses says he will persist until reaching the meeting of the seas or traveling a long time, setting the strenuous search whose lost-fish turn is identified in 18:64. | terra: Moses vows not to cease moving until he reaches the junction of the two seas even if he travels for ages, a direct Quranic scene of the section's seeker who will not stand still or abandon the search.

luna: The source section illustrates seeking through a lost animal; this neighbor says the fish was forgotten and took its way into the sea, supplying the loss that Moses and his companion recognize as their sought sign in 18:64. | terra: At the sought junction Moses and his companion lose notice of their fish as it takes a path into the sea, supplying the missing-object event that drives the search scene through 18:64.
terra: After passing the junction, Moses asks for food and names the journey's fatigue; this ayah registers the exertion and overshooting that lead to retracing their steps in 18:64.

luna: The source section's lost-camel example turns on finding what has disappeared; here the companion recalls the fish's strange path into the sea, the clue that makes Moses identify what they were seeking in 18:64. | terra: The companion recalls the forgotten fish and its strange path into the sea, identifying the lost sign and the place to which the seekers must return.

luna: The source section illustrates ب غ ي/B001 with seeking a lost camel; after Moses and his companion lose the fish (18:61, recalled in 18:63), they say «ذلك ما كنا نبغ» and retrace their steps, a lost-creature search that leads to their intended meeting. | terra: Moses says ذَٰلِكَ مَا كُنَّا نَبْغِ and they return عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَارِهِمَا قَصَصًا; what they sought is recovered by turning back and following their own tracks.

luna: The source section says the search ends in meeting the sought one; this ayah names «لقاء ربه» as the hope of the one who does righteous work, giving that meeting a devotional condition. | terra: Whoever hopes to meet his Lord must act rightly and keep worship unmixed, so the anticipated encounter governs the purity of the seeker’s present direction.

luna: The source section contrasts the seeker with the denier who turns away; here Moses and Aaron warn Pharaoh of punishment for «كذب وتولى», giving that paired rejection its own stated consequence. | terra: The warning that punishment is upon مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ exactly repeats the section's paired denial and turning away.
terra: فَتَوَلَّىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُۥ ثُمَّ أَتَىٰ shows Pharaoh depart, gather his plan, and return, a clear bodily-departure sense of tawallī directed to a hostile purpose.
terra: God's question “What made you hasten from your people, Moses?” identifies the directed haste whose goal and desired رضى Moses states in 20:84.
terra: Moses says وَعَجِلْتُ إِلَيْكَ رَبِّ لِتَرْضَىٰ: his people are on his track, he hastens directly toward his Lord, and the movement ends in sought pleasure.
terra: وَعَنَتِ ٱلْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَىِّ ٱلْقَيُّومِ lets “faces” stand for whole persons humbled before the living, sustaining Lord.
terra: Whoever turns away from God's remembrance receives a constricted life and is raised blind, making loss of attention in the present become loss of sight at the end.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to glorify his Lord through the recurring turns of day and night لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَىٰ, linking persevering orientation to eventual satisfaction.

luna: The source section pairs a face directed toward God with turning away; this person «انقلب على وجهه» when tested, depicting a reversal of direction whose aim had never been firm. | terra: The person who worships God on an edge is settled by benefit but, when tested, turns back on his face and loses both worlds; the face reveals an unstable direction governed by immediate satisfaction.
terra: A group says it believes and obeys, then يَتَوَلَّىٰ after that; the change exposes turning away as abandonment of professed obedience.
terra: When summoned to God and His messenger for judgment, a group becomes مُعْرِضُونَ, supplying the actual call they refuse after the turn named in 24:47.
terra: The believers' answer سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا supplies the exact opposite of the refused hearing and obedience staged in 24:47-48.
terra: Those who neither hear nor reason are likened to livestock and said to be further astray in path, joining animal behavior, failed hearing, and lost direction.
terra: The Messenger asks no payment except that whoever wills take a path to his Lord, joining absence of human recompense with a freely chosen Godward direction.

terra: When the staff appears as a snake, Moses وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ: he turns and runs without looking back, a precise bodily use of the root and a reversal of the wild animal that stops to look behind.
terra: Moses sets himself toward Midian and asks his Lord to guide him to the even way; directed movement, the face-root, and hoped-for guidance form one travel scene.
terra: The second telling repeats that Moses وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ, confirming bodily flight without a backward turn as a distinct form of tawallī.

luna: The source section names ب غ ي/B001 as seeking with effort; this verse commands seeking the Hereafter through what God gave while forbidding seeking corruption, contrasting the proper object of pursuit with a corrupt one. | terra: The ayah places وَٱبْتَغِ the Hereafter opposite وَلَا تَبْغِ corruption on earth, using the same root for two incompatible objects and making direction decisive.

luna: The source section identifies God's face with God Himself; «كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه» makes that reading concrete by setting the enduring divine face against the perishing of everything else. | terra: كُلُّ شَىْءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجْهَهُ makes God's face the sole exception to universal perishing, clarifying why seeking that face gives the search an enduring end.
terra: Whoever hopes for the meeting with God is assured that God's appointed term is coming, supporting the section's movement from sustained seeking to encounter.
luna: The source section describes ابتغاء as effortful seeking; here striving for God is answered by His guidance to His ways, tying exertion to the direction found.

luna: The source section's face-direction image is repeated in «فأقم وجهك للدين حنيفا»; this ayah anchors turning toward religion in the created disposition, adding an account of why that direction fits the human being. | terra: فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا repeats the command to set one's face firmly toward the upright religion and associates that orientation with God's created pattern.

luna: The source section's wording ابتغاء وجه ربه is directly matched by giving to kin, poor, and traveler for those who desire Allah's face; the verse makes face-seeking a motive for concrete generosity. | terra: Giving the relative, needy person, and traveler their due is identified as good for those يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَ ٱللَّهِ, making concrete the section's giving as a direction toward God's face.

luna: The source section joins seeking God's face with giving; this verse contrasts wealth meant to multiply through usury with charity given seeking Allah's face, whose increase is with Him. | terra: The ayah contrasts an outlay intended to grow through people's wealth with zakat given تُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَ ٱللَّهِ; the sought face determines whether giving is self-returning or Godward.
terra: The repeated command أَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ ٱلْقَيِّمِ adds urgency: establish the face's direction before a day that cannot be turned back.

luna: The source section explains turning away as either bodily withdrawal or abandoning attention; this ayah depicts a person who turns away arrogantly from recited signs as if he had not heard, the secondary sense made visible.
terra: The prohibition against turning one's cheek from people uses literal face posture to expose pride, a human-scale boundary on how bodily orientation carries moral meaning.

luna: The source section reads God's face as the sought Lord Himself; «أسلم وجهه لله» describes surrender to Him, and its firm-handhold image shows the stability of that orientation. | terra: Whoever يُسْلِمْ وَجْهَهُۥٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ has grasped the firm handhold, and the ayah ends with all outcomes returning to God; direction and destination coincide.
terra: Those who deny renewed creation are described as disbelieving in the meeting with their Lord, directly negating the encounter at which the section's search ends.
terra: The answer to the denied meeting in 32:10 states that death will take them and then they will be returned to their Lord, restoring the destination they reject.

luna: The source section's image includes turning away from what one is called to heed; this ayah asks who is more unjust than one reminded of the Lord's signs and then «أعرض عنها». | terra: The wrongdoer is one reminded of his Lord's signs who ثُمَّ أَعْرَضَ عَنْهَا, a concise nonbodily turn away from received instruction.
terra: Those who had covenanted not to يُوَلُّونَ ٱلْأَدْبَٰرَ show how a bodily turn of the back can also violate an inward commitment.
terra: A man comes running from the farthest part of the city to urge his people to follow the messengers, supplying directed and urgent movement for the no-payment and guidance claim in 36:21.
terra: The command to follow messengers who ask no payment and are rightly guided joins freedom from worldly recompense to a trustworthy direction.

terra: The running believer asks why he should not worship the One who originated him and to whom all will be returned, giving the movement of 36:20 and unpaid guidance of 36:21 their final destination.
terra: Abraham says إِنِّى ذَاهِبٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّى سَيَهْدِينِ, making physical departure an image of going toward the Lord under His guidance.
terra: God does not يَرْضَىٰ disbelief for His servants but is pleased with gratitude, placing denial and رضى on opposite sides of the same moral turn.

luna: The source section describes turning toward the Lord as the sought orientation; this command says «أنيبوا إلى ربكم وأسلموا له», making return to God a response before punishment arrives. | terra: وَأَنِيبُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمْ وَأَسْلِمُوا۟ لَهُ commands a turn toward the Lord before punishment arrives, the positive reversal of tawallī as departure.
terra: On the Day of Resurrection the faces of those who lied about God are blackened, bringing the face and the act of lying together in their final visible consequence.
terra: The warned day is one when people turn their backs fleeing, with no protector from God, and the ayah closes by contrasting divine misguidance with the absence of any guide.

luna: The source section explains turning away as refusing to listen; after the Quran is presented as good news and warning, most «فأعرض أكثرهم فهم لا يسمعون», matching that secondary sense in a preaching scene. | terra: Most people turn away from the Quran's good news and warning so that they do not hear, an exact instance of the section's nonbodily turn through failed listening.

luna: The source section connects turning away with leaving attentive listening; here disbelievers tell one another not to listen to the Quran and to make noise over it, an explicit effort to block hearing.

luna: The source section says the face turns toward God Himself; this verse forbids prostration to sun or moon and directs worship to their Creator, a clear boundary between a sign and the One sought.
terra: The same repeated image—turning away and distancing by one's side after blessing—shows how a body's orientation can disclose a settled stance.
terra: God chooses whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back, again expressing guidance as a Godward reorientation.

luna: The source section's root ب غ ي/B001 means seeking; this ayah distinguishes seeking the harvest of the Hereafter, which God increases, from seeking the world's harvest, which has no share in the Hereafter.

luna: The source section describes turning away by refusing to listen or comply; this ayah depicts someone who hears God's signs, then persists arrogantly as if he had not heard, and warns of punishment.
terra: The disbelievers turn away from the very warning addressed to them, another clear case of departure accomplished by refusing reception rather than by moving the body.
terra: People who turn back after guidance has become clear show a backward direction chosen after the route is already known.
terra: Those condemned اتَّبَعُوا۟ مَآ أَسْخَطَ ٱللَّهَ وَكَرِهُوا۟ رِضْوَٰنَهُ: their following has the wrong direction, and anger is set against the pleasure they reject.
terra: The ayah first identifies those who withhold when called to spend and then warns that if the community turns away God will replace it, gathering miserliness and tawallī in one address.

luna: The source section ends with the seeker pleasingly content; here Allah is pleased with believers as they pledge allegiance beneath the tree, connecting divine approval to a concrete act of commitment.
terra: The believers seek God's bounty and pleasure while the mark of prostration is on their faces; sought approval, bodily orientation, and face are visibly joined in one ayah.
terra: Pharaoh فَتَوَلَّىٰ بِرُكْنِهِ and dismisses Moses as magician or madman, joining a posture of turning with verbal refusal of the message.
terra: فَفِرُّوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ gives flight a destination in God, reversing the fleeing animal whose movement is defined only by what it leaves behind.

luna: The source section sets seeking the Lord's face against turning away; this person «تولى عن ذكرنا» and wants only the near life, making the rival object of that turn explicit. | terra: The Prophet is told to turn from one who تَوَلَّىٰ عَن ذِكْرِنَا and wants only worldly life; the object desired exposes why that person's face is directed away.
terra: The question أَفَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِى تَوَلَّىٰ introduces a turner whose interrupted giving is specified in the next ayah.
terra: وَأَعْطَىٰ قَلِيلًا وَأَكْدَىٰ depicts giving a little and then stopping, reversing both the generous act and the persistent search developed in the section.

luna: The source section glosses ب غ ي/B001 as seeking and says ابتغاء entails effort; this ayah states that a person has only what he strives for, making the effort itself the basis of the eventual outcome.
luna: The source section describes exertion in seeking; following 53:39's account of striving, this ayah says the effort will be seen, adding its disclosure before recompense in 53:41.
luna: The source section ends with the seeker's future contentment; following 53:39-40, this ayah says the effort will be repaid in full, completing the sequence from striving to outcome.
terra: When the people see a sign they turn away and dismiss it as continuing magic, so visual reception immediately becomes bodily and interpretive refusal.
terra: The command فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ shows that turning away can also be a divinely commanded withdrawal from entrenched deniers, a boundary on treating every bodily turn as blameworthy.

luna: The source section says the sought face remains; this neighbor states «كل من عليها فان», the passing condition that 55:27 sets against the enduring face of the Lord. | terra: كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ gives the universal passing-away against which the remaining face of the Lord in 55:27 becomes visible.

luna: The source section explicitly says the sought face endures; «ويبقى وجه ربك» states that permanence, while 55:26 supplies the contrast that all on earth pass away. | terra: وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ states that the Lord's face remains, grounding the section's identification of the face with God Himself and the lasting object of the search.
terra: The world's growth and fading are set against severe punishment, forgiveness, and pleasure from God in the Hereafter, locating lasting satisfaction beyond what visibly flourishes and passes.

luna: The source section's root ب غ ي/B001 is effortful seeking and its final word يرضى names contentment; here people adopt monasticism «ابتغاء رضوان الله», but the ayah says they did not maintain it as required, distinguishing intention from fulfilled obedience. | terra: Monasticism was invented ٱبْتِغَآءَ رِضْوَٰنِ ٱللَّهِ but was not observed as it should have been; intended seeking is tested by whether effort remains faithful to its object.

luna: The source section's sought face means God Himself; here Allah says He is pleased with those whose faith and loyalty are firm even against opponents of God and His Messenger, tying approval to allegiance. | terra: Those whose faith withstands opposing loyalties receive gardens and the mutual verdict رَضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا۟ عَنْهُ, a communal form of the search's satisfying end.

luna: The source section's wording seeks God's face through giving; these emigrants leave homes and wealth «يبتغون فضلا من الله ورضوانا», a concrete cost-bearing pursuit of divine approval. | terra: The poor emigrants leave homes and wealth while يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضْوَٰنًا, making costly physical displacement an enacted search for divine approval.

luna: The source section presents seeking God as a single direction; this ayah names those who go forth striving and «ابتغاء مرضاتي», then forbids taking as allies those who oppose that aim. | terra: The believers' claimed going out in God's path and ٱبْتِغَآءَ مَرْضَاتِى is tested against secret affection for His enemies, making the sought approval govern the direction of loyalty.
terra: The Torah-bearers are likened to a donkey carrying books and then called people who كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ, joining an animal image, failed reception, and denial in one ayah.
terra: The same obedience formula ends with فَإِن تَوَلَّيْتُمْ and the Messenger's duty of clear conveyance, a repeated nonbodily use of turning away.

terra: The phrase تَبْتَغِى مَرْضَاتَ أَزْوَٰجِكَ uses the same search-for-pleasure construction with human approval as its object, marking a boundary around seeking that overrides what God made lawful.
terra: The blazing fire calls مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ, making backward movement and turning away the very orientation that carries a person toward the threatened fire rather than the sought face.
terra: The one called by the fire جَمَعَ فَأَوْعَىٰ, gathering and hoarding; this supplies the withholding practice paired with the turn in 70:17 and reverses Godward giving.
terra: Noah says his repeated invitation only increases his people's flight, preparing the concrete gestures of blocked hearing and concealment in 71:7.
terra: Each time Noah calls his people toward forgiveness, they put fingers in their ears, cover themselves, persist, and grow proud; refusal to hear is rendered as a sequence of bodily evasions.

luna: The source section says turning away can mean abandoning heed and obedience; this verse describes the one who turns away from remembrance of his Lord and the punishment that follows. | terra: Whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord is led into mounting punishment, making the turn's destination explicit.

terra: وَلَا تَمْنُن تَسْتَكْثِرُ may mean not to give expecting an increase; on that reading it is a specific boundary against the return-seeking gift opposed by 92:19-20, though the wording also permits other readings.
luna: The source section couples denial with turning away; this man «ثم أدبر واستكبر», and 74:24 supplies the dismissive claim that the warning is only inherited magic, completing the rejection.

luna: The source section pairs denial with turning away and develops an animal image for the denier; this ayah asks why people turn away from the reminder, before 74:50-51 compare them to fleeing donkeys. | terra: فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ ٱلتَّذْكِرَةِ مُعْرِضِينَ names the people's aversion from the reminder before the next two ayat render that aversion as animal flight.

luna: The source section's dictionary sense for ك ذ ب/B007 describes a wild animal running and looking back; this ayah compares people turning from the reminder to alarmed donkeys, a specific fleeing-animal parallel, though it does not show the source's backward glance. | terra: كَأَنَّهُمْ حُمُرٌ مُّسْتَنفِرَةٌ turns the avoiders into startled wild donkeys, a close Quranic counterpart to the section's dictionary image of the wild animal embedded in denial.

luna: The source section's dictionary sense for ك ذ ب/B007 uses a wild animal running before it stops to look back; this ayah says the donkeys flee from a lion, echoing flight from a threat but not the pause or backward look. | terra: فَرَّتْ مِن قَسْوَرَةٍ supplies the fleeing motion that completes the animal analogy for turning away from the reminder.

luna: The source section ends in رضى, contentment; the radiant faces in «وجوه يومئذ ناضرة» belong to the following ayah's people who look toward their Lord (75:23), giving that end a visible expression. | terra: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَّاضِرَةٌ places radiant faces at the opening of the encounter completed in 75:23.

luna: The source section ends with seeking God and becoming content; here the faces of the saved look toward their Lord, while 75:22 describes those faces as radiant, picturing the encounter behind the image. | terra: إِلَىٰ رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ gives those faces a single object of gaze—their Lord—making literal the section's image of a face kept toward what it seeks.

luna: The source section ends with the seeker pleased; this neighboring judgment scene contrasts radiant faces looking toward the Lord in 75:22-23 with «وجوه يومئذ باسرة» expecting calamity. | terra: Gloomy faces on that Day form the visual counterpart to the radiant faces looking toward their Lord in 75:22-23.

luna: The source section's search culminates in contentment; this neighbor completes the contrast begun in 75:24 by showing those faces expecting a crushing calamity. | terra: Those gloomy faces expect a back-breaking calamity, giving their gaze an opposite anticipated end from the Lordward gaze of 75:23.

luna: The source section locates the dying denier's conduct in the moment when life reaches the collarbones; this ayah supplies that threshold scene before 75:31-32 name his failure to affirm and his turning away.

luna: The source section says the search ends in meeting the sought Lord; this adjacent death passage says that on that day the drive is to the Lord, giving the dying scene in 75:26 and 75:31-32 its destination.

luna: The source section contrasts the denier who turns away with the giver who seeks God; this ayah says the condemned man neither affirmed nor prayed, while 75:32 supplies the matching denial and turning away. | terra: فَلَا صَدَّقَ وَلَا صَلَّىٰ states the negative counterpart to 92's affirmation of the best and prepares the explicit كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ of 75:32.

luna: The source section places the turn-away person against the one who seeks God's face; here the dying person's «كذب وتولى» is the same paired rejection, while 75:31 separately says he did not affirm or pray. | terra: وَلَٰكِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ repeats the exact pair and makes bodily departure from the truth the culmination of the refusal described in 75:31.

luna: The source section's example of seeking God's face through feeding appears in 76:9; this ayah identifies the recipients as poor, orphan, and captive, giving that generosity its concrete scene. | terra: Feeding the needy person, orphan, and captive despite love of the food supplies the concrete gift whose sole motive and refusal of repayment are voiced in 76:9.

luna: The source section's phrase ابتغاء وجه ربه is directly echoed by the feeders' «لوجه الله»; their refusal of recompense or thanks sharpens the section's account of giving without seeking a human return. | terra: The feeders say their gift is only لِوَجْهِ ٱللَّهِ and seek neither repayment nor thanks, the closest parallel to 92:19-20's unrecompensed gift and sought face.

luna: The source section says the donor expects no human return; after the words of 76:9, these givers explain that they fear a grim day from their Lord, identifying the motive behind their unstated reward.
luna: The source section ends in the seeker's contentment; after the giving described in 76:8-10, God protects these people from that day's evil and gives them radiance and joy.
luna: The source section describes ابتغاء as strenuous seeking and ends with رضى; this passage concludes the feeding-and-worship account by calling the reward given and the effort appreciated.
terra: فَكَذَّبَ وَعَصَىٰ gives Pharaoh's denial and disobedience, the stance whose bodily direction and strenuous movement appear in 79:22.
terra: ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ يَسْعَىٰ shows a man striving while headed away, the exact reversal of the section's tireless seeker whose face remains on the goal.

luna: The source section contrasts turning away with seeking God's face; here a man «عبس وتولى» from the blind visitor seeking guidance, and 80:10 says the speaker became distracted from him, showing that turning away can be interpersonal neglect. | terra: عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ stages tawallī as an interpersonal bodily turn, with the next ayah identifying the person from whom the face was turned.
terra: أَن جَآءَهُ ٱلْأَعْمَىٰ gives the arrival of the blind man as the occasion of the turn in 80:1 and makes the bodily movement morally legible.
terra: The deniers are veiled from their Lord on that Day, a precise boundary and reversal of the section's search ending in encounter with the sought face.

luna: The source section says its root ب غ ي/B001 means seeking and that ابتغاء carries effort; here the human being labors toward his Lord and meets Him, joining exertion to the encounter the section says ends the search. | terra: إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا فَمُلَاقِيهِ turns a lifetime of strenuous movement toward the Lord into an eventual meeting, matching the section's search ending face to face.

luna: The source section directs the seeker toward the Lord and says His face remains; this ayah states the contrary preference for the near life, while 87:17 says the Hereafter is better and more enduring.
luna: The source section says the sought face endures; this neighboring ayah calls the Hereafter better and more lasting, completing the contrast with preference for the near life in 87:16.
terra: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَّاعِمَةٌ introduces blessed faces whose inward result is specified by their satisfaction in the next ayah.
terra: لِّسَعْيِهَا رَاضِيَةٌ makes the faces of 88:8 satisfied with their striving, bringing face, effort, and رضى together as the section does.

luna: The source section describes the turn-away person alongside a caller to heed; this ayah tells the Messenger to remind, and 88:22-23 clarify that he cannot control people who then turn away and disbelieve.

luna: The source section says guidance is not the Prophet's responsibility; this ayah states he is not set over people as a controller, immediately before 88:23 names those who turn away and disbelieve.

luna: The source section's turning-away figure also denies; «من تولى وكفر» states that pair and leads into punishment in 88:24, while this ayah itself marks the boundary between reminder and refusal. | terra: إِلَّا مَن تَوَلَّىٰ وَكَفَرَ identifies turning away and disbelief as the opposite stance to the satisfied faces earlier in the same surah.
luna: The source section's final ayah promises contentment; this call to the tranquil soul introduces the return in 89:28, where it is both pleased and approved.

luna: The source section ends «ولسوف يرضى»; here the soul returns to its Lord «راضية مرضية», and 89:29-30 complete the welcome by admitting it among the servants and into Paradise. | terra: ٱرْجِعِىٓ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَّرْضِيَّةً combines return toward the Lord with being pleased and pleasing, a compact version of directed movement ending in mutual acceptance.
luna: The source section's search ends in meeting and contentment; after the pleased soul returns in 89:28, this ayah welcomes it among God's servants, completing the reception.
luna: The source section ends with the seeker's future رضى; following the return and welcome in 89:28-29, this ayah names entry into God's garden as the consummating reward.
terra: وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ closely echoes 92:21's promise in wording and cadence while making the Lord's giving the cause of the promised satisfaction.
terra: وَوَجَدَكَ ضَآلًّا فَهَدَىٰ reverses the lost-animal illustration: here God finds one without the way and supplies guidance, making the seeker also one who has first been found.

luna: The source section's paired words كذب and تولى recur in the man who denies and turns away while trying to forbid a servant's prayer; the concrete obstruction shows what refusal to heed looks like. | terra: أَرَءَيْتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ applies the exact denial-and-turning pair to the man who tries to stop a servant from praying.

luna: The source section ends with the human seeker becoming content; «رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه» makes the relation reciprocal and gives its setting as gardens beneath which rivers flow. | terra: The best creatures receive lasting gardens and reciprocal pleasure, and the ayah links that end to one who fears his Lord, clarifying whom the promised رضى belongs to.
